stories.headline: Eagles' Broadway jab at Titans leads NFL Week 2 trolls
stories.summary: Teams across the NFL came with petty postgame energy after wins in Week 2, led by the Philadelphia Eagles.
stories.body:
With half of the league looking to remain undefeated heading into Week 2, a win could lead to an even sweeter troll. Case in point? The Philadelphia Eagles.

The Eagles used a late two-minute drive to steal a 24-20 win against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville.

Tennessee took a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left and needed one stop for its first win of the season. But Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts led his team down the field with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with a 3-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Darius Cooper with nine seconds left. It marked the Eagles' latest winning passing touchdown since 2012, according to ESPN Research.

Nashville is home to the famous Broadway Street, but Philadelphia has its own notable street too: "Broad Street." Therefore, the Eagles posted a graphic of an Eagle on a "Broadway" street sign but covered "way" with a sticky note that read: "Street," putting a spin on Nashville's area.

Here are more of the top trolls from NFL Week 2.

Carolina Panthers 34, Atlanta Falcons 3
Carolina defeated its NFC South foe on the road Sunday in convincing fashion.

Panthers quarterback Bryce Young passed for 287 yards and three touchdowns, two of which went to tight end Darren Waller. Carolina forced five turnovers -- three interceptions and two fumbles -- as Atlanta had only 286 total yards of offense.

Carolina's blowout win came with an equally dominant social media performance. It first shared a victory post with the score and caption: "Feelin' Peachy," a reference to Georgia being known as the Peach State. The Panthers then posted a graphic of a Panther eating a bird's egg with the caption: "We cooked."

New Orleans Saints 24, Baltimore Ravens 17
The Saints faced a 17-9 deficit heading into the fourth quarter but responded with consecutive touchdowns -- the final one coming with 1:28 left. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw an interception on the ensuing drive, and New Orleans secured the victory.

The NFC South team directed its troll toward an unlikely source: a Baltimore fan who had choice words for Saints fans on X. They wrote that Saints fans were "talking crazier than Colts fans," the Ravens' Week 1 opponent, and they'd similarly learn the "hard way" like Indianapolis' followers. Baltimore defeated Indianapolis last Sunday.

New Orleans remembered the slight, quoting the post with a video of wide receiver Chris Olave celebrating his fourth-quarter touchdown with the caption: "Love those crazy Saints fans."

Minnesota Vikings 9, Chicago Bears 3
Another divisional game brought another troll, this time from the Minnesota Vikings.

Minnesota kept Chicago in check after the Bears put up 59 points in a Week 1 victory. The Vikings forced two turnovers, including one as Chicago running back D'Andre Swift fumbled while diving for a touchdown. The Bears reached the red zone again but had a field goal attempt blocked with 6:23 left. Minnesota got one more stop to claim the win.

The Vikings kept it simple after the victory. They shared a "W" graphic with the caption: "WINdy City DUB," emphasizing the "win."

San Francisco 49ers 35, Miami Dolphins 13

San Francisco is off to a dominant start to the season with consecutive double-digit wins -- this time against Miami.

The 49ers erupted in the third quarter with three touchdowns, two of which were delivered by quarterback Brock Purdy. Running back Christian McCaffrey added the final one after he had a score in the first quarter. Purdy threw for 287 yards and and completed 91% of his pass attempts with 30 rushing yards and a score. He's the first player with 250 passing yards on 90% completion and 30 rushing yards in a game in NFL history.

Consistently petty, San Francisco had trolls lined up postgame for Miami. The 49ers referenced the Dolphins' namesake, referred to making "a splash" and posted an image of a dolphin pool float.

Las Vegas Raiders 26, Los Angeles Chargers 14

The Raiders are 2-0 for the first time since 2021 after a big win against the Chargers.

Las Vegas pulled ahead in the fourth quarter behind consecutive turnovers by Los Angeles -- a fumble by running back Omarion Hampton then an interception thrown by Justin Herbert. Hampton's fumble resulted in a Raiders touchdown to put them up 10 with 2:59 remaining. Las Vegas quarterback Kirk Cousins had 259 yards passing and three touchdowns, and wide receiver Tre Tucker led the team with five receptions for 119 yards and a score.

A massive victory came with a straight forward troll as -- not far from Hollywood -- the Raiders captioned their win post: "Roll credits." As Cousins walked off the field, he took a video thanking the fans who showed up at Sofi Stadium and said it "felt like a home game," which Las Vegas wrote in its caption.

Seattle Seahawks 31, Arizona Cardinals 7

It has been almost 10 months since Seattle lost a regular-season or postseason game, and Arizona is the latest to be on the other end of a victory.

The Seahawks outscored the Cardinals 24-0 in the second half behind a stellar performance from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The wide receiver had nine catches for 155 yards and three touchdowns. He has scored Seattle's first four touchdowns of the season, becoming only the second player in NFL history to record each of his team's first four-plus touchdowns of the season, according to Elias Sports Bureau.

And like the Seahawks have done during their win streak dating to last season, they made sure to troll their opponent. They first shared a comic of their mascot posing in front of a buried Big Red, the Cardinals' mascot. Seattle then posted an image of a burnt tortilla with a "W" grilled on it and the caption: "That's a wrap."

Cleveland Browns 23, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 19

The Browns are in the win column following a late defensive stand against the Buccaneers.

Lightning delayed the game by 2 hours, 12 minutes, resuming while Tampa Bay held possession at the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The Buccaneers had a chance to take the lead on fourth-and-11 with 22 seconds left. But quarterback Baker Mayfield threw an interception and Cleveland came up with a clutch victory.

The Browns poked fun at the Buccaneers' classic "Bucco Bruce" logo postgame, sharing a meme that pointed at Bruce and asked: "What does he even do?"

stories.headline: Sources: Higuain at center of refs' union beef with MLS NEXT Pro
stories.summary: The union that represents MLS and USL referees launched a scathing critique of MLS NEXT Pro over its handling of an incident in which a coach committed what it described as "two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism towards a female official."
stories.body:
The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), the union that represents MLS and USL referees, launched a scathing critique of MLS NEXT Pro over its handling of an incident in which a coach of an MLS NEXT Pro team committed what it described as "two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism against a female official."

Multiple sources told ESPN that the coach in question is Columbus Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain.

In a social media post that didn't reference Higuain by name, the PSRA said that the acts consisted of squeezing the hand of the official "and refusing to let go after being told to stop three times." The post added: "This physical intimidation was compounded by a demeaning, sexist remark to the official, 'Don't forget that this is a man's game.'"

Multiple sources told ESPN that the incident occurred during the postgame handshake immediately following Crew 2's Aug. 23 match against Huntsville City FC. Higuain received a red card for the incident.

MLS NEXT Pro conducted an investigation, which resulted in Higuain being suspended for two games and ordered to take part in restorative practice training. A source added that Higuain has begun but not yet completed the training and has already served the two-game suspension.

At issue for the PSRA is that the punishments weren't severe enough. In its social media post, the PSRA said that U.S. Soccer policy mandates a minimum three-game suspension for a "forceful grab" and that acts of discrimination also require a minimum three-game suspension.

"The League's response falls drastically short of the right message to the participants, the referees, and the public. It needs to be reevaluated," the PSRA's social media post read.

In a statement to ESPN, MLS NEXT Pro said the league "immediately investigated the reported incident between the head coach and the female official. It was determined that the coach's behavior violated League policies and warranted additional discipline beyond the red card that was issued in the moment. He served a two-game suspension and is required to participate in a multi-session restorative practices process, which is already underway. The program is intended to support the League's efforts to foster understanding, accountability, respect, and the restoration of relationships across the League. MLS NEXT Pro believes in the restorative approach. The League is confident in its process and the results."

The Crew also sent the following statement to ESPN: "The Crew actively collaborated with MLS NEXT Pro throughout the review process and fully accepted the additional discipline issued in accordance with league policies.

"Our Club is dedicated to growing the game by creating environments where everyone is welcome and supported on and off the pitch, which is founded upon our values of respect, inclusivity and prioritizing people and culture first. We condemn any action or notion that contradicts our mission of uniting and uplifting all communities and genders through the global game."

As for why a heavier punishment wasn't meted out, one source with knowledge of the league's thinking indicated that the league believes the minimum suspension spelled out in U.S. Soccer policies is a guideline and not mandatory.

The U.S. Soccer policy manual is explicit on the matter of penalties for assault toward referees. Policy 202-2 Section 2 of the U.S. Soccer Policy manual, dated May 2026, states that "All Professional League Members shall adopt and enforce policies prohibiting misconduct against referees that meet the following minimum criteria."

The policy goes on to state that, "Any player, coach, manager, club official, or league official who commits an intentional act of physical violence at or upon a referee ('Referee Assault') shall be suspended without pay for a period of at least six consecutive matches (the "Assault Suspension"). The Assault Suspension shall commence with the first match after which the individual has been found to have committed this act."

Assault is defined in the U.S. Soccer Policy manual as including, but not limited to: "striking, kicking, choking, grabbing or bodily running into a referee; spitting on a referee with ostensible intent to do so; kicking or throwing an object at an official that could inflict injury; or damaging the referee's uniform or personal property (e.g., car, uniform, or equipment)."

The manual also states that "The Professional League Member may not provide for a penalty shorter than the Assault Suspension but may provide for a longer suspension and/or a fine."

The U.S. Soccer Policy manual says the minimum suspension for referee abuse -- defined as "verbal and nonverbal communication which contains foul or abusive language and which implies or directly threatens physical harm; spewing a beverage on or spitting at a referee or the referee's personal property" -- is three games.

Caleb Pongratz of Spotrac was the first to report that Higuain was the coach involved in the incident.

stories.headline: ESPN's Brownlow Medal predictor and tracker - every vote for 2026
stories.summary: The Brownlow Medal is the highest individual honour in the AFL. In 2026, ESPN is giving you an advantage with our one-of-a-kind predictor.
stories.body:
The Brownlow Medal is the highest individual honour in the AFL. In 2026, ESPN is once again giving you an advantage with our unique predictor, which has correctly picked eight out of the past 12 winners, as well as 80% of all top 10 finishers in that time.

Most Brownlow Medal predictors use a standard 3-2-1 voting structure, mirroring the votes awarded by the umpires after each game. ESPN's system, however, does things a little differently. A player can be allocated 3, 2.5, 2, 1.5, 1 or 0.5 votes per game, resulting in a much lower margin for error.

For example, in a game where it's difficult to split two players for best on ground honours, this system would give 2.5 votes to each, as opposed to one being given 3 and the other receiving 2. Over the course of the season, the difference between the predictor and the actual votes a player tallies will likely be much closer, and therefore more accurate. There are still six votes allocated to players per game.

stories.headline: Washington Mystics beat Indiana Fever 93-77, move within 1 game in standings
stories.summary: — Kiki Iriafen scored 21 points and grabbed 14 rebounds to help the Washington Mystics beat Indiana 93-77 and pull within a game of the fifth-place Fever.
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- — Kiki Iriafen scored 21 points and grabbed 14 rebounds to help the Washington Mystics beat Indiana 93-77 and pull within a game of the fifth-place Fever.


Shakira Austin added 20 points with 10 boards for the Mystics (26-16), who are one of three teams just a game behind Indiana (27-15) with two regular-season games remaining. The Fever finish with a home-and-home series on Tuesday and Thursday against the Minnesota Lynx, owners of the WNBA’s best record at 32-10.


Sonia Citron scored 16 points and just missed a double-double with nine assists. Georgia Amoore had 11 points with three 3-pointers.


The Mystics jumped out to a 34-19 lead at thge end of the first quarter. They led by as many as 26 before closing the half with a 51-30 advantage. Washington was up 77-61 entering the fourth and never were threatened.


Caitlin Clark scored 25 with five assists and Kelsey Mitchell had 22 points for the Fever. But the All-WNBA backcourt shot a combined 14 of 40 from the floor, including making just 6-of-20 3-pointers.


Fever All-Star center Aliyah Boston encountered foul trouble and scored just seven points on eight shots. And Indiana's bench didn't contribute a point until Raven Johnson's jumper with 4:35 remaining in the third quarter.


UP NEXT


Mystics: Host Connecticut on Tuesday.


Fever: Host Minnesota on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Raptors honor Kyle Lowry with golden 'GROAT' statue
stories.summary: Lowry also received a key to the city of Toronto and a special dinner to honor his contribution to the franchise.
stories.body:
With a sea of red, white and black Kyle Lowry jerseys filling the streets of Toronto for an honorary block party, the guard's legacy will forever be stamped in the city's lore with an exclusive commemorative figure.

On Saturday, the Toronto Raptors honored Lowry's career with a block party outside of Scotiabank Arena, unveiling a golden raptor statue. The sculpture features Lowry's No. 7 jersey while dribbling a basketball and stands on a nameplate that reads "The Greatest Raptor of All Time. Kyle Lowry | 2012-2021, 2026."

The statue unveiling follows the franchise's August announcement that it would retire Lowry's jersey number during the upcoming 2026-27 season. It will be raised to the rafters at the conclusion of Toronto's home matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers on Jan. 10.

Along with the statue, the six-time All-Star received a key to the city.

"I've been looking forward to this moment for years. I always said that Toronto is home, and that I'd retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me," Lowry said. "We built something special here -- my teammates, the organization, the city and the fans, and all of Canada. We became champions together, and to be able to share this night with all of them, and with my family, is going to mean a lot to me."

Lowry, who spent nine of his 20 seasons in Toronto, helped bring the Raptors their only NBA championship in the 2019 NBA Finals. He will also join Basketball Hall of Famer Vince Carter as the only Raptors to have their numbers retired -- Carter's was retired in November 2024.

The 40-year-old Lowry announced his retirement in July after signing a one-day contract with Toronto to retire as a member of the franchise.

He averaged 13.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and six assists in his 20 seasons.

stories.headline: UFC 331 takeaways: Are we living in the greatest era for lightweights?
stories.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Joshua Van stole the show with emphatic statements at UFC 331.
stories.body:
The main card of UFC 331 had shocking moments on top of shocking moments on top of pound-for-pound resume building.

First, Sean Sharaf got his first UFC win as the biggest underdog in the promotion's history against Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds. Then Arman Tsarukyan stepped into the cage for the first time this year and reminded everyone why the current crop of UFC lightweights may be the best ever. And flyweight champion Joshua Van followed it all up with a performance that should place him among the 10 best MMA fighters in the world right now. What more could an MMA fan want?

Van is a top five pound-for-pound fighter
I can't believe I'm saying this -- not because Van isn't great or hasn't been great for some time. It's just -- how does one become a top-five fighter in the world at age 24, with less than five years of pro experience?

After his performance on Saturday, I can't talk about Van anymore as just a phenom or a young champion. He is legitimately as good as just about anyone in the entire sport. Alexandre Pantoja coming off injury looked like the same Pantoja as before the injury. If anything, he looked even more determined than before. His pressure was appropriate and his decision-making was sound. Van was just better.

He defended takedowns and escaped on the ground when Pantoja could get him there. At one point, was it just me or did Van catch Pantoja's glove as he threw a punch, before countering? He caught some of Pantoja's kicks, in the same way he caught the one in December that led to Pantoja's injury. In the fifth round, when the result of the fight still felt up in the air, Van delivered his best five minutes of work, dropping Pantoja with a right hand.

Van is gifted athletically, confident and a natural finisher. He's been all of that from the first moment we saw him. One description that shouldn't be forgotten, however, is that he's extremely technical. This was one of the most technical fights of the entire year, against one of the best flyweights of all time, and Van ended up running away on the scorecards. If Van were 28, I don't think anyone would have an issue ranking him near the top of the pound-for-pound. The only hesitancy to do it is because -- it doesn't seem right or possible, given his age and relative inexperience. I'm getting over that. Van is top five. -- Brett Okamoto

Are we living in the greatest lightweight era of all time?

The history of the UFC's lightweight division is so undeniably rich. One of the division's greatest "eras" was from 2016 to 2020, when Conor McGregor became double champ at Madison Square Garden, Khabib Nurmagomedov dominated and timeless fighters such as Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje were in their primes.

This upcoming chapter at lightweight has a chance to challenge all that.

Within the past three months, Ilia Topuria has suffered his first loss (in spectacular fashion to Gaethje on the White House lawn) and vowed revenge. Paddy Pimblett has turned in a star-making performance, submitting Benoît Saint Denis in less than a minute on a McGregor-headlined card. And now Arman Tsarukyan has completed an unbelievable walkoff knockout of Mauricio Ruffy. Topuria, Pimblett and Tsarukyan are three legitimate superstar storylines, and it just so happens they are all rivals who have promised to take each other out.

Don't forget that the champion, Gaethje, could postpone retirement in order to defend his throne. Veterans Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira are still active in the top five, too. Australia's Quillan Salkilld has had a breakout year, and Nurmagomedov's younger cousin, Usman, could potentially transition to the UFC after years of dominance in the PFL.

Yeah. The next few years could be the best in lightweight history, and that is really, really saying something. -- Okamoto

The Steveson train has hit an early crossroads

It's not like Steveson had never lost before. On his way to becoming a 2020 Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was formidable but not perfect. His record at the University of Minnesota was 103-3. His international freestyle record, including cadet and junior levels, was 53-2. Even an all-time great has had to pick himself up and dust himself off at times.

But this defeat was different from whatever Steveson had ever experienced. He got knocked out cold in 12 seconds by Sharaf, a guy who came into their fight 0-2 in the UFC with both losses coming by knockout. Let's just acknowledge that this matchmaking was a setup to build an MMA résumé for Steveson. Considering that he had just four pro fights under his belt, though, this was an appropriate booking.

The result was a shocker. It was the largest known upset in UFC history, per DraftKings. But what's done is done, and the story now takes an unexpected twist. Will this be just a speed bump on Steveson's express road toward the top of the UFC heavyweight division? Or will this defeat make Steveson timid in standup fighting, slowing his development beyond being a one-dimensional wrestler? Heavy-handed UFC heavyweights will surely be emboldened by seeing Steveson crash to the canvas. What seemed like a sure thing now is surrounded by question marks. The future might still be bright for Steveson. It probably will be. Here's a suggestion for Steveson: Don't bother watching the 12-second KO loss. Why put yourself through that again? Instead, go find video of Islam Makhachev's 2015 KO loss in his second UFC fight, then contemplate how Makhachev has managed to win all 17 of his fights since on his way to becoming the best pound-for-pound fighter in the sport. -- Jeff Wagenheim

stories.headline: Azerbaijan Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Baku, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.

Title leader Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the drivers' championship after picking up his eighth victory of the season at the brand-new Madring last time out.

He leads his teammate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now dropping back in the title race after a retirement in Spain.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 15th race of the season.

- Madring's F1 debut left everyone dissatisfied, even Spanish GP's top 3

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Azerbaijan Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, September 24

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Friday, September 25

Final Practice: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Saturday, September 26

Azerbaijan Grand Prix: 12 p.m.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the race on a Saturday?
For the first time in Baku's history, the F1 weekend will shift a day forwards, with the race taking place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijan National Day of mourning on the Sunday.

Azerbaijan's people will dedicate their thoughts to military personnel and those who died during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.

Baku City Circuit

After the European leg of the calendar where circuits are more traditional, Baku is one of the standout street circuits of the season.

The first race in Baku was held in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before it was called the Azerbaijan Grand Prix a year later.

The section around Turns 8, 9 and 10 are lined by the walls of the city's charming old town including a castle and the long main straight along the Baku shoreline sees cars reach speeds in excess of 220 mph and is the best spot for overtaking.

The walls are narrow and the high-speeds make for either a race full of chaos, or none at all. There is a 57% chance of a Safety Car being deployed during the race.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Circuit: Baku City Circuit; Baku, Azerbaijan

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2024: Oscar Piastri (McLaren)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2016 European GP. (First race as Azerbaijan GP in 2017)

Laps: 51 laps of 6km.

Lap record: 1:43.009, Charles Leclerc (2019).

Most wins: Pérez (2021, 2023) and Verstappen (2022, 2025) with two wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2018), Bottas (2019) and Piastri (2024).

Most poles: Leclerc with four (2021-2024) and Hamilton (2017), Bottas (2019) and Verstappen (2025) are the other pole sitters from the current grid.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be dry and sunny throughout the weekend. Temperatures will be around 26°C, but will drop to 24°C for the race on Saturday.

What happened last year?
Red Bull's Verstappen took pole position around the streets of Baku in a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags.

He ended up converting that pole into a dominant victory, with Russell in second and Carlos Sainz behind.

It was a key moment in the championship fight between Lando Norris and Piastri as Norris closed the gap to 25 points to his McLaren teammate after the Australian crashed out.

Who will win this year?

The last street circuit this year was in Monaco in June and since then several of the top teams have upgraded its packages and haven't yet gone racing on street circuits, but Baku has now arrived.

Antonelli has looked on fire in the last two races, but Norris is creeping to the front. The reigning world champion has two wins to his name in Hungary and Zandvoort, but also suffered an unlucky run in Madrid with the safety car deployment, so missed out on a potential win there as well.

Mercedes are set to be quick in the high-speed straight lines in Baku, but the tight and twisty corners might suit Ferrari and McLaren best.

One of the main aims will be to not crash the car into the wall otherwise the whole course of the race can rapidly change in a blink of an eye.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Updated: NRL 2026 team-by-team season review
stories.summary: The 2026 NRL season proper has come to an end, so it's time to evaluate every team's year.
stories.body:
The 2026 NRL season proper has come to an end, so it's time to evaluate every team's year. We take a look back at our preseason prediction, assess the way each team travelled, and work out their grades for 2026.

This will be updated as every team's season finishes.

Brisbane Broncos
Last year's ladder finish: 4th (Premiers)

Predicted 2026 finish: 3rd

Actual finish: 14th

Grade: F

Very rarely does a premiership winning side fall so far, so quickly. Everyone fully expected that the Broncos would mount an impressive title defence on the back of what they achieved in 2025 and the relative stability of their squad. What the pundits and fans could not predict was the behind-the-scenes discourse, the injuries to key players, and the apparent complete lack of commitment from players out in the middle. The coach losing the locker room is an often-used excuse, usually followed by the sacking of the coach, but Michael Maguire was only in his second season at the club after bringing them premiership glory in his first year. The players have to be held accountable for this unsightly collapse.

Where to from here: Adam Reynolds has retired, Payne Haas is off to the Rabbitohs, and the talk is that the players are not happy with coach Maguire. Mitch Barnett is coming to replace Haas, Dane Gagai to shore up the backline, and Jonah Pezet to reset the halves. They have the entire offseason to sort themselves out, a similar season in 2027 would be completely intolerable for the proud club.

Canberra Raiders
Last year's ladder finish: 1st

Predicted 2026 finish: 7th

Actual finish: 11th

Grade: D

The Raiders took out the minor premiership last season, but the way they crashed out of the finals was not encouraging when it came to predicting their 2026 run. They still should have played finals football this year and, as they showed against the Cowboys in the final round, they still have all the weapons to challenge the top sides. Hudson Young's injury certainly didn't help as they battled for a spot in the Top 8, nor did their ability to lose games they had seemingly already won.

Where to from here: They have lost several players ahead of next season, without making any moves on the player market. They will rely on the juniors coming through as well as halfback Coby Black, who lived up to all the hype during his debut performance against the Cowboys in the final round.

Canterbury Bankstown Bulldogs
Last year's ladder finish: 3rd

Predicted 2026 finish: 2nd

Actual finish: 12th

Grade: F

The Bulldogs receive an F for their 2026 season, simply because they were expected to build on their 2025 success, not crumble in the opposite direction. Lachlan Galvin proved that he is a star of the near future and probably the club's best player through the year, but he played halfback when the team needed a genuine halfback. Moving Matt Burton to centre saw him improve with new found freedom out wide, but moving Stephen Crichton to five-eighth hamstrung his best assets. The whole team continued to look completely lost in attack and only finished as high as they did through defensive resolve, which also faded at the back end of the season. Such a disappointing effort.

Where to from here: Freddy Lussick arrives to hopefully fix one part of the spine. Either Mitchell Woods or Alex Conti should be ready to pull on the No. 7 jersey, Galvin will rise to star status wider of the ruck in the No. 6 jersey, and Burton and Crichton can form the most expensive and lethal of centre combinations. All the club needs then is an attack coach, a dangerous fullback, a new lock and some more grunt in the front row. Easy!

Cronulla Sharks
Last year's ladder finish: 5th

Predicted 2026 finish: 10th

Actual finish: 5th

Grade: C

The Sharks receive a C because they were expected to take a tumble down the ladder after another disappointing finals series last year, but rallied through the season to finish fifth. There were times when they looked certain to finish in the Top 4, but lost their way near the end when Braydon Trindall was injured. They struggled with consistency, looking like world beaters for chunks of the season, but totally lost at other times. Addin Fonua-Blake once again proved his worth to the team, but could have used a bit of help. Nicho Hynes and Trindall worked really well together in the halves and Blayke Brailey was always sharp out of dummy-half. If anything their outside backs started to look a little tired and in need of a freshen up. They limped into the finals in the middle of a slump from which they never really recovered.

Where to from here: The Sharks are putting a broom through the roster, without making any major recruitment moves. Gone are Sione Katoa, Mawene Hiroti, Cameron McInnes, Jesse Ramien and Siosifa Talakai, with a couple of Super League imports their main gains. They will rely on their pathways to develop the young talent needed to build their 2027 starting team. The glory days of 2016 drift further into the past with each disappointing season.

Dolphins
Last year's ladder finish: 9th

Predicted 2026 finish: 6th

Actual finish: 3rd

Grade: TBD

Where to from here: TBD

Gold Coast Titans
Last year's ladder finish: 16th

Predicted 2026 finish: 14th

Actual finish: 16th

Grade: D

We predicted the Titans would improve slightly under coach Josh Hannay, but they stayed in exactly the same spot. It must be so frustrating for everyone involved to watch the patches of sensational football this club is capable of playing at times. Jayden Campbell remains an elite attacking weapon, Keano Kini an amazing young talent at fullback, Cooper Bai an explosive forward and Tino Fa'asuamaleaui a stoic leader. But, they just lack a couple of key pieces and the drive to play a full 80 minutes of totally committed football.

Where to from here: Apart from welcoming Sharks centre Mawene Hiroti in 2027 they haven't made too many moves on the player market and will be looking instead to improve their systems and fitness. Hannay has a long road ahead of him, with the Bears joining the fray next season, the Titans will face another rung on that ladder they failed to climb at all in 2026.

Manly Sea Eagles
Last year's ladder finish: 10th

Predicted 2026 finish: 13th

Actual finish: 9th

Grade: C

The Sea Eagles started the season where they left off in 2025, losing and looking like a team headed down the ladder. They sacked Anthony Seibold and hired club legend Kieran Foran as head coach and went on an incredible run, which looked certain to take them into the finals. They lost Tom Trbojevic to injury and managed to keep going, but subsequently losing Luke Brooks brought the winning run to a grinding halt. Overall it was a very mixed year, which ended in a frustrating ninth place finish.

Where to from here: They lose Reuben Garrick to the Roosters next year and have made some minor acquisitions. Foran will have a full offseason with the side and they have some promising talent coming through at the club including halfback Joey Walsh. It will be interesting to see whether Foran can recapture the magic of his early days in the job, as they battle again to play finals football.

Melbourne Storm
Last year's ladder finish: 2nd (Runners-up)

Predicted 2026 finish: 8th

Actual finish: 10th

Grade: D

We tipped the Storm to take a slide down the ladder after losing last year's grand final to the Broncos, but no one ever really expects them to miss the finals. They did have a horror year with injuries, with their superstar spine seldom complete for any number of consecutive games. When they did have Harry Grant, Jahrome Hughes and Cameron Munster they were capable of beating anyone, but the bit-part players were unable to lift in their absence. Injuries aside, the Storm didn't look like the Storm at times, with defensive lapses and handling errors driving coach Craig Bellamy up the wall.

Where to from here: Bellamy is going around again as coach, which is handy as it would have been an injustice for him to leave the Storm after that season. They are revamping their backline with the addition of Dolphins flyer Jamayne Isaako and Bulldogs centre Bronson Xerri, while adding Eels forward Kelma Tuilagi. They are also losing a raft of players including Tyran Wishart and Nick Meaney, both to the Bears.

Newcastle Knights
Last year's ladder finish: 17th

Predicted 2026 finish: 13th

Actual finish: 7th

Grade: TBD

Where to from here: TBD

New Zealand Warriors
Last year's ladder finish: 6th

Predicted 2025 finish: 9th

Actual finish: 2nd

Grade: B-

Considering we expected the Warriors to miss the finals, for them to be challenging the Panthers for the minor premiership right until the final round makes this a successful season and worthy of a B. The way they crashed out of the finals in straight sets, very nearly drops them back to a C. How disappointing for Warriors fans everywhere to see them fall to the Dolphins and Knights in front of adoring home crowds. Their efforts against the Knights in front of a packed Eden Park will haunt them for many years to come. They had trouble all season keeping a starting pair of halves fit, but managed to finish second on the ladder with Chanel Harris-Tavita and Te Maire Martin working well together. Their pack, led by James Fisher-Harris, was one of the most destructive in the league, but they just weren't able to put it all together in the big games, when it really mattered.

Where to from here: The Warriors lose a raft of players, led by Mitch Barnett, Luke Metcalf and Marata Niukore. They welcome outside backs Will Warbrick and Grant Anderson, with prop Sam McIntyre also joining from the Cowboys. Coach Andrew Webster has done an incredible job with the club, but he has clearly not unlocked the secret to having them perform to their best on the biggest of stages. If anything, their first premiership seems further away after that finish.

North Queensland Cowboys
Last year's ladder finish: 12th

Predicted 2026 finish: 16th

Actual finish: 8th

Grade: C

The fact that the Cowboys somehow snuck into the finals was enough for them to receive a C for their efforts this year. Wildly inconsistent, they could switch on the magic and just about beat anyone, but their defence was appalling at times and ultimately costly. They entered their elimination final needing to tighten up their defence and cut back on their errors, but fell down in both areas. Fullback Scott Drinkwater had a night to both forget and savor in the elimination final against the Sharks, setting up several Cowboys tries while looking completely lost under the high ball.

Overall they got to play in one more game than nine other teams, without ever seriously looking likely to threaten for the title. Their home fans might well remember the season for it's ultimate lowlight: the Round 22 loss to the Roosters which finished in a club record 82-12 flogging.

Where to from here: Scott Drinkwater departs for the Dragons, as the Cowboys go through a minor clean-out. They welcome Joe Chan (Storm), Sione Katoa and Jesse Ramien (both Sharks). Coach Todd Payten will need to spend the entire offseason working on defensive schemes and instilling some commitment to the cause.

Parramatta Eels
Last year's ladder finish: 11th

Predicted 2026 finish: 12th

Actual finish: 13th

Grade: D

The Eels had a frustrating season, often competitive, but rarely consistent. When they were bad, they were very bad, conceding 52 points to the Storm in the opening round, before conceding another 52 to the Titans just five weeks later. They weren't helped by injuries to Mitchell Moses and one-year halves partner Jonah Pezet, but were more often let down by a lack of defensive resolve. Beating the Sharks in Round 26, only to lose to the Dragons in the final round, just about summed up 2026 for the Eels and their long-suffering fans.

Where to from here: They lose a bundle of players for next year, while acquiring Jarome Luai from the Tigers and Jaydn Su'A from the Dragons. It is hard to make any sense of the one-year deal for Luai, even more so with the late-season form of Ronald Volkman, but maybe he will click with Moses and provide more value to the Eels than he did for the Tigers. It is certainly going to be an interesting season for the Eels.

Penrith Panthers
Last year's ladder finish: 7th

Predicted 2026 finish: 1st

Actual finish: 1st

Grade: TBD

Where to from here: TBD

St George Illawarra Dragons
Last year's ladder finish: 15th

Predicted 2026 finish: 17th

Actual finish: 17th

Grade: D

Nailed it. Pre-season favourites for the wooden spoon, the Dragons lived up to all the hype. A mid-season coach sacking didn't help them as much as it did the Sea Eagles, with Dean Young struggling to squeeze any consistency out of the team. We saw flashes of brilliance from Tyrell Sloane, Jacob Liddle and the Dragons' young forward pack, but nothing short of lethargy at times from players like Valentine Holmes, Moses Suli and Clint Gutherson. When in the right mood, they provided some moments of tough opposition, but doing it week-to-week for a full 80 minutes was beyond them.

Where to from here: Nothing but exciting times ahead for the Dragons as they welcome one of the most bountiful player market raids in the history of rugby league. Scott Drinkwater (Cowboys), Keaon Koloamatangi (Rabbitohs), Luke Metcalf (Warriors), Kodi Nikorima (Dolphins), Phillip Sami (Titans) and Connor Watson (Roosters) will all be joining the Dragons' ever-improving young forwards for what should be a complete transformation. Line up now for those 2027 finals tickets, Dragons fans!

South Sydney Rabbitohs
Last year's finish: 14th

Predicted 2025 finish: 5th

Actual finish: 6th

Grade: C

We expected the Rabbitohs to play finals football and considering the injury issues they suffered through the year, they deserve a C for achieving that goal. It was a little ironic then that their season came to an end largely due to yet another injury, this time to Cody Walker. Walker was the spark that fired up Souths' attack all year, without him they were flat and no match for the energetic Knights. Latrell Mitchell's return at the end of the season was definitely a boost; Cameron Murray was his dominating best around the ruck; and Alex Johnston was busy setting try-scoring records on the wing. There were some questions over whether coach Wayne Bennett was best utilising the talents of Jye Gray through the season, with Matthew Dufty disappointing at times at fullback. It was a disappointing end to what was a very promising season.

Where to from here: Payne Haas arrives from the Broncos next season to joining David Fifita in one of the NRL's most intimidating forward packs. They do lose Keaon Koloamatangi from that pack, but Haas is well established as the best forward in the world. The Rabbitohs will squeeze one more season out of Cody Walker, if they can come to an agreement on how much he is worth. Going on their exit from the finals without him, he is just about priceless.

Sydney Roosters
Last year's ladder finish: 8th

Predicted 2025 finish: 4th

Actual finish: 4th

Grade: TBD

Where to from here: TBD

Wests Tigers
Last year's finish: 13th

Predicted 2026 finish: 7th

Actual finish: 15th

Grade: F

What a horribly disappointing season for Tigers fans everywhere. The re-built club, with Jarome Luai at the helm, were expected to break their finals drought and started strongly beating the Cowboys, Warriors, Knights and Raiders in the first eight rounds. And then, Luai announced he was signing with the PNG Chiefs for the club's debut 2028 season. The Tigers imploded and it has been a long road of misery since, conceding 52 to the Sharks, 44 to the Storm, 46 to the Sea Eagles, 68 to the Panthers and 56 to the Raiders along the way. They did upset the Roosters in Round 25 to bring a little joy to the black-and-gold army.

Where to from here: Coach Benji Marshall has to somehow wipe 2026 from the players' minds, as he focusses their attention on returning to finals football in 2027. They have made two very astute acquisitions in Jake Averillo (Dolphins) and Jayden Brailey (Raiders). Both are no-nonsense professionals who will sharpen up the Tigers' play and their attitude.

stories.headline: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes
stories.summary: Rounding up the top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
stories.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Sunday night drip
Indianapolis Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner might have had the best outfit ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Buckner wore a navy and black silk suit made by Gentleman's Playbook. It was a bold and unique choice.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce also showed up in style with a Louis Vuitton collarless jacket and matching belt. His teammate, Patrick Mahomes, rocked Adidas from head to toe with Oakley sunglasses.

Here are the top fits ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens kept it simple up top, with a pop of color below for his arrival ahead of a divisional game against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Pickens wore a solid black T-shirt, multicolored striped shorts, and purple-and-black Nike Dunks on the feet.

Commanders' rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was among the best dressed players during the arrivals for the Sunday afternoon games. Styles arrived in a grey suit, with his initials embroidered on the collar in gold.

Here are more notable arrivals from the 4 p.m. slate:

Best of 1 p.m. arrivals
Cincinnati Bengals defensive lineman Myles Murphy was the best dressed during Sunday's early slate. Murphy arrived wearing a Gallery Department Logan canvas trucker vest with black cargo pants. His Bottega Veneta woven duffle bag was a strong complementary piece.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was dressed to impress, arriving for a home game against his former team, the Cleveland Browns. Mayfield wore a cream polo with khaki and green striped and white shoes.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson wore a red letterman jacket and loose-fit khaki pants ahead of a road matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Here are some of the other memorable fits from Sunday's 1 p.m. slate:

Thursday night's best fit

To kick off Week 2, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb arrived in a plaid Archival button-down shirt paired with dark denim jeans.

stories.headline: White Sox keep pace in the AL Central with a rain-soaked 8-1 win over the Tigers
stories.summary: — Sam Antonacci had a two-run double in a three-run fourth inning and the Chicago White Sox kept pace in the AL Central and eliminated the Detroit Tigers from playoff contention with a rain-soaked 8-1 victory Sunday.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — Sam Antonacci had a two-run double in a three-run fourth inning and the Chicago White Sox kept pace in the AL Central and eliminated the Detroit Tigers from playoff contention with a rain-soaked 8-1 victory Sunday.


The White Sox remained a game behind the Cleveland Guardians in the division and hold a three-game lead over the Houston Astros and Toronto Blue Jays for the third wild card.


The start was delayed 3 hours, 50 minutes by rain and most of the game was played in a swirling mist.


Davis Martin threw 4 1/3 scoreless innings for the White Sox, striking out six, allowing three hits and walking three. He failed to record a win for his 15th straight appearance dating to June 10.


Huascar Brazoban (6-2), activated from the injured list earlier Sunday, pitched a scoreless sixth for the victory.


Trevor Richards pitched two innings for the 205th White Sox relief outing of 1 1/3 innings or more, a major league record.


Braden Montgomery started the scoring with an RBI double in the second. Kyle Teel singled home Antonacci after his double in the fourth. Chase Meidroth hit his 15th home run in the fifth, a two-run shot into the left-field bullpen.


Max Clark broke up the shutout with a sacrifice fly in the top of the eighth.


Detroit reliever Brant Hurler walked in a run in the bottom of the inning and Randal Grichuk followed with a sacrifice fly to make it 8-1.


Detroit starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed three runs on four hits and three walks in 3 2/3 innings before leaving with a trainer after Antonacci's double.


Eduardo Valencia had three hits for the Tigers.


Up next
The Tigers have not announced a starter for Monday's opener of a three-game series against Washington. The White Sox are off Monday before before beginning a three-game series at Kansas City, with LHP Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.41 ERA) starting Tuesday against LHP Daniel Lynch IV (6-6, 3.29).

stories.headline: AFL overreactions: Lachie Neale should play in the Grand Final
stories.summary: Lachie Neale is facing a ban for his gut punch on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan. If it's upheld at the tribunal, the Lions star misses the Grand Final. But should he get off? It's time to react to the week's big talking point.
stories.body:
There are plenty of talking points after the AFL's preliminary final weekend, with the biggest being whether Brisbane Lions star Lachie Neale deserves his one-week ban for a gut punch on Jack Ginnivan, which, as it stands, has the two-time Brownlow Medal winner missing the 2026 Grand Final.

Let's get to this week's overreactions column, where we judge the biggest takeaways as legitimate or irrational.

Lachie Neale should get off, and play in the Grand Final
Brisbane superstar Lachie Neale is set to miss the AFL Grand Final against Fremantle after being handed a one-game ban for striking Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan during Saturday evening's thrilling preliminary final at the MCG.

Minutes after the league handed down the verdict the Lions released a statement confirming the club would be challenging the suspension at the tribunal. So, should the ban stand or should Neale be free to help his side to a historic threepeat?

Jake Michaels
Verdict: Not an overreaction

I've been one of Neale's greatest supporters and advocaters throughout his entire football career, but come on, the man simply cannot take to the field on Saturday afternoon.

Neale knew what he was doing. He ran up behind Ginnivan, swung his fist with serious force into his stomach and dropped him to the ground. It was stupid. It was unnecessary. It was a brain fade of the highest order. And just like everyone else, he simply must cop the penalty that we all know fits the crime.

This year alone, there have been six instances of players being handed suspensions for similar off-the-ball gut punches -- that non-football action the league has been desperate to stamp out of the game and remove from all levels of grassroots football. What sort of crappy example would it set by downgrading the suspension to a fine and allowing Neale to play?

I understand Brisbane's desire to challenge the decision and pray their star midfielder is able to play, but the league must stand firm on this. It's an incredibly slippery slope if we start making concessions simply because it's Grand Final week. The tribunal needs to stand firm and not cave to the external pressure.

Matt Walsh
Verdict: Overreaction

I didn't think I'd be saying this, but missing a Grand Final for something -- in the grand scheme of things -- that is relatively minor would be a shame.

Yes, it would be upheld as a ban if it was in Round 10. Yes, he should know better. But put plainly, it'd suck to not have one of the biggest five names in the sport taking to the field on Grand Final day for something that would have resulted in a fine last year, you can't deny that.

I'd like to see a greater threshold for missing a Grand Final. Think of it like the 'reverse double demerit' argument. In order to miss a Grand Final, you have to have done something significant. It's a Grand Final! A silly moment shouldn't keep you out of the biggest game of the year.

Is it double standards? It sure is, but you could point out a handful of incidents every week which 'coulda, shoulda, woulda' when it comes to the MRO and the tribunal. Neale's incident was not significant enough to warrant missing a decider.

It happens with the Brownlow, too. Think Patrick Cripps' hit on Callum Ah Chee which was overturned at the tribunal after a marathon hearing. It was thrown out on an 'error of law' and Cripps wasn't embarrassed on Brownlow night. And you know what? We all got over it.

Neale's hit on Ginnivan wasn't high and he wasn't left concussed. I think he's stiff. Stupid, but stiff.

stories.headline: UFC 331 results: Van dominates Pantoja to retain men's flyweight title
stories.summary: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan earned big wins on a contender for fight card of the year. Here are the UFC 331 highlights.
stories.body:
If there were any doubts about Joshua Van's championship mettle, they were put to bed after his dominant victory over Alexandre Pantoja in the UFC 331 main event at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Saturday night.

Van outstruck Pantoja and successfully defended double-digit takedown attempts and even dropped Pantoja in Round 5 en route to a unanimous decision win to retain the UFC men's flyweight title over the former champion.

Pantoja put up a good fight, as he held his own on the feet and racked up nearly 10 minutes of control time. His best showings were in Rounds 1 and 4, when he got a hold of Van and successfully took the fight to the mat. But Van did enough to get a win on the judges' scorecards. He has now defended his title twice.

In the co-main event, Arman Tsarukyan earned what could be the biggest win of his career, putting knockout artist Mauricio Ruffy to sleep with an elbow in Round 1. The win likely cements Tsarukyan as the top contender for UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Also on the main card, heavyweight Sean Sharaf pulled off an all-time UFC upset, knocking out top prospect Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds.

Brett Okamoto, Jeff Wagenheim and Dre Waters break down all the action from Los Angeles.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton shuts down asking Ferrari to make changes: 'Never asked for anyone to be replaced'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eight world championship is over.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eighth world championship is over.

Hamilton threw in the title towel at last weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after he retired from the race in Madrid with a brake problem.

His failure to finish leaves him 101 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings -- the equivalent of more than four victories -- with just nine scheduled rounds left.

A report in Italy claimed Hamilton has challenged Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur to make changes to the team's trackside staff.

But in a story posted to his Instagram account on Thursday, the 41-year-old wrote: "I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up on here.

"I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves.

"I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

- Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Hamilton sparked hope of challenging Antonelli -- the driver who replaced him at Mercedes -- when he won in Barcelona in June.

However, the British driver has not finished on the podium at the past five rounds and has been openly critical of his team's race tactics.

He also took aim at teammate Charles Leclerc's driving after an opening-lap clash in Monza earlier this month. Hamilton said he led face-to-face talks with the Monegasque to clear the air.

His retirement in Madrid marked his first of the campaign, and when asked to assess his title chances, Hamilton replied: "There's no stopping him [Antonelli] and Mercedes this year. They've done a phenomenal job, and they deserve it [the championship]."

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: 'We're not done': Ponga, Knights plot Penrith upset
stories.summary: Kalyn Ponga has declared there are more chapters to write in Newcastle's revival story as the 2025 wooden spooners aim to upset Penrith to make the grand final.
stories.body:
Kalyn Ponga insists now is not the time for nostalgia as Newcastle's captain aims to move a step closer to completing one of the great NRL revivals by taking the Knights to the grand final.

After Sunday's drama-charged 12-10 win over the Warriors in Auckland, Newcastle's Cinderella finals run will extend into another week with Justin Holbrook's set to face Penrith in a preliminary final at Accor Stadium.

Fullback Ponga will feature after he passed the head injury assessment which left him watching the dying stages of the win over the Warriors from the dressing room.

Victory over the Panthers this Sunday would count as the Knights' biggest scalp to date and would cap the club's remarkable turnaround from wooden spooners to grand finalists in the space of 12 months.

The Roosters were the last side to finish last (2009) and reach the decider the following year.

But captain Ponga claims he has no desire to look back on the Knights' rapid progress under first-year Newcastle coach Holbrook as he believes there are more chapters to write.

"It's kind of hard right now because you're obviously grateful for the win but then you don't want to sit in that for too long," Ponga said.

"You want to get your mind to the next game, and that's been our strength this year.

"I think when it's all said and done, when we're sitting at home in the off season, I'll look back and be pretty proud of this season.

"But it's kind of hard right now because we're not done.

"All I do know is I'm really proud of this group for the efforts that they've put in throughout the whole year. I don't want to reflect too much just yet."

The Knights had the luxury of giving representative forward Dylan Lucas a cameo in the final 20 minutes of the win in Auckland and his return from injury will be a major boost for a side that has stumbled into September without a handful of big hitters.

Newcastle have survived into week three without their first-choice front-row duo of Jacob Saifiti and Trey Mooney and have thrived in attack despite the absence of injured star playmaker Dylan Brown.

"The belief sort of comes from the year. You go into these games relying on what you've done throughout the year," Ponga said.

"So many times we've had injuries, had to overcome adversity and challenges, and as a playing group, we've handled that pretty well. No doubt it'll be the same next week."
